title: MOST HOLY, LIKE THE SIN OFFERING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"It must not be baked with yeast; I have given it as their share of the food offerings presented to me. Like the sin offering and the guilt offering, it is most holy."'" - Lev 6:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
I have given it as their share. God calls the priests' food a gift.

The priests could easily have seen it as a wage — payment for services rendered, something earned by their labour at the altar. God corrects the framing before it starts. This is not your salary. This is My gift.

That distinction protects the heart. A person who thinks he has earned what he receives becomes entitled, and resentful when it falls short. A person who knows he has been given something becomes grateful.

We need this correction constantly. We speak of "my" income, "my" home, "my" health, as though we generated them. Moses warned Israel about exactly this danger before they entered the land: You may say to yourself, "My power and the strength of my hands have produced this wealth for me." But remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth (Deut 8:17-18).

Every good and perfect gift is from above (Jas 1:17).

Look at whatever you are most proud of having achieved. Then look again, and count how many things had to be given to you before you could achieve it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of what I have as earned or as given?
2. What have I taken credit for that was actually God's provision?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, everything I call mine was first Yours and then Your gift. Replace my sense of entitlement with gratitude. Amen.
